title: App Fair submission
description: One app in the App Fair catalog: which repository and tag to build, how it is built, and where it is published. One file per app under apps/, named for the app token, in YAML. scripts/queue.py enforces this shape along with the rules in policy.yaml; this document is here so an editor can complete and check the file as it is written.

token.description: The app token: the name of its GitHub organization and repository (the app lives at https://github.com/<token>/<token>), the file name here, and the last segment of its bundle id (org.appfair.app.<token>). It holds for the life of the app.

title.description: The name people see on their device and in the store. Unique in the catalog.

tag.description: The released tag to build. It names the version being published, so the app at that commit has to build the same X.Y.Z. The checks refuse a branch name here.

commit.description: The commit that tag points at, in full and in lower case. Every stage checks this out, so moving the tag afterwards does not change what is published. `scripts/queue.py resolve` prints it.

id.description: The bundle id this app publishes under, when it is not org.appfair.app.<token> — an app keeps the id its store records were created under by writing it here. Any id the stores accept is allowed; the check is only that the app builds the id this file names. Play takes this id with hyphens as underscores unless android-id says otherwise.

android-id.description: The package name this app publishes under on Google Play, when it is not the bundle id with hyphens as underscores. A Java package name: two or more segments, each starting with a letter, no hyphen.

summary.description: One line about the app for people reading the catalog. The stores show the listing from the app's own repository.

distribution.description: Where this app is published, keyed by the target that builds for it. Each target is built once and each channel under it gets a submission. policy.yaml declares the channels; apple-app-store and google-play-store work today.

android-mdc.description: The channels that take the android-mdc package.

ios-uikit.description: The channels that take the ios-uikit package.

apple-app-store.description: Settings for the apple-app-store channel, for an app whose distribution sends it there.

submit.description: Whether this channel is asked to review and distribute the build. Defaults to true, which is what publishing means. Set it to false to upload the build and leave it alone: on the App Store that leaves the version in Prepare for Submission, and on Play it lands in the internal track as a draft.

profile-secret.description: The NAME of the repository secret holding this app's base64 App Store provisioning profile, when it differs from the catalog's default. The profile itself belongs in the secret.

google-play-store.description: Settings for the google-play-store channel, for an app whose distribution sends it there.

Set it to false to upload the build and leave it alone: on the App Store that leaves the version in Prepare for Submission, and on Play it lands in the internal track as a draft.

altstore.description: Settings for the altstore channel, for an app whose distribution sends it there. This channel is planned; the queue cannot publish to it yet.
